description:
1. Artifact claim. This deposit is the v1.2 preprint PDF of The Governance Patch-Gap: Machine-Speed Exploit Discovery Against Human-Speed Legal Repair. It defines the governance patch-gap as the rate ratio G = Rd/Rp and a stock S with dS/dt = Rd − Rp: AI collapses the cost of discovering legal open texture while repair stays on a legislative clock. Prefer concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21910874 for always-latest PDF.

2. Problem / scientific context. Legal systems are Highly Optimized Tolerance (HOT) artifacts: drafters optimize against anticipated disputes, so residual fragility concentrates in Hart's penumbra (open texture), not in the core. Three threat actors (corporate optimizer, state actor, misaligned autonomous agent) occupy that penumbra. Discovery and execution are separate governance problems. G is a definition, not a fitted dynamical model; regime labels (G ≈ 2, 102, 103+) are heuristics.

3. Contents. Single PDF PAPER_PATCHGAP-REL.pdf. Markdown source lives at github.com/chokmah-me/patch-gap. No simulation code in this deposit. Companion software is a separate Zenodo concept (10.5281/zenodo.21918091; this zip 10.5281/zenodo.23262639).

4. Reproduce. The PDF is not executable. Definitions and §4.4 arithmetic are gated in the companion repository (python run_all_gates.py). Five-audience TL;DRs live in tldr.md.

5. Relation to other records. Paper concept 10.5281/zenodo.21910874. This version supersedes v1.1 10.5281/zenodo.21924075. OSF archive node osf.io/w96xz is a legacy mirror; Zenodo is canonical. Catalog: chokmah.me.

6. Limitations / non-claims. G is a definition. Regime magnitudes are order-of-magnitude heuristics. SocioHack is a sandbox preprint without independent replication (judge κ = 0.55 in v1, 0.86 in v3 under a different protocol). A1/VERITE is 36 already-vulnerable contracts. Rice / FLP / attestation in §6.4 are analogical extensions. The BCBSA hospital-coding case in §5.4 is an auxiliary signal, not a resolution of Prediction 2: $942M is the total two-year figure, of which $653M came from 55k+ secondary-diagnosis cases; attribution is from a payer association, not an enforcement record.

TL;DRs for different audiences

For the SME.
Legal systems are HOT artifacts: residual fragility concentrates in Hart's penumbra. The object is a rate ratio G = Rd/Rp and a stock S with dS/dt = Rd − Rp; G is a definition, not a fitted dynamical model. Regime labels are heuristics. SocioHack is unreplicated; A1/VERITE is 36 already-vulnerable contracts. Rice / FLP / attestation in §6.4 are analogical. The load-bearing claim that survives if SocioHack fails is the work-factor collapse in adjacent formal systems plus the discovery/execution split.

For the interested layman.
Laws have always had gray zones on purpose — words like "reasonable" so judges can handle new cases. Finding those gray zones used to be slow and expensive. AI can search the whole tax code and regulation pile cheaply and flag gaps nobody has noticed. Passing a fix still takes months to years. The paper names that mismatch the governance patch-gap: machines find holes faster than legislatures and courts can close them. The holes were always there. What changed is the cost to find them.

For the practitioner.
Treat "AI found a loophole" and "an agent filed on it" as different problems. Discovery is a tool-governance issue (access, disclosure, audit of comment corpora). Execution is an agency-and-liability issue (who is the principal; HITL above a dollar / classification / cross-border threshold). Disclosure mandates reach corporate repeat players and miss unsupervised agents. Do not spend the policy budget on formalizing "reasonable"; Catala-class work shrinks the core, not the penumbra. Immediate moves: require AI-use disclosure in filings and litigation; log agent actions that change regulatory classification.

For the decision maker.
This is not a model-refusal problem and will not be closed by a better system prompt. The asset at risk is the stock of known-but-unpatched legal ambiguities. Adjacent formal systems (smart-contract exploit agents at $0.01–$3.59/attempt; attacker break-even ~$6k vs defender ~$60k) already show the cost collapse. Near-term: rate-limit execution (HITL, disclosure). Do not buy "formally verified law" as a complete close.

For governance.
Every new AI rule written in open-textured natural language is another search surface. Three defenses, all bounded: (1) AI red-team of draft text before enactment — useful, not exhaustive; (2) formal methods — core only; (3) rate-limits — buy time, do not close G. Conflating corporate optimizers, state arbitrage, and unsupervised agents produces the wrong instrument. Falsifiers: AI-authored substantive rulemaking comments by end-2027; an attributed in-production exploit by end-2027; two governments or the EU publishing legislative red-team reports by mid-2028. All three remain open as of October 2026.
